chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, he raised it (to the Imam), he said:
The Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked: 'When should I strike my beast?' He said: 'When your riding does not travel as fast as it travels to its feeding trough.'
ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to strike an animal according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a precise metric for animal welfare, defining the threshold of permissible discipline as the animal's natural, unburdened pace to its feeding trough. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on *adl* (justice) in treatment, prohibiting riders from striking the beast merely to force a speed exceeding its innate comfort, thereby preventing unnecessary suffering and ensuring the animal is not treated as a mere tool of coercion.
